chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the woman who is in prayer and thinks that she has menstruated, he said: She should insert her hand and touch the place. If she sees something, she leaves (prayer), and if she does not see anything, she completes her prayer.

key_terms.الْمَوْضِعَ: The place (referring to the area of menstruation)

ai.seo_question: What should a woman do if she suspects her period has started while praying?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) in the context of ritual purity, where the absence of confirmed blood validates the ongoing validity of the prayer. It highlights the practical Shia juristic approach of distinguishing between mere suspicion (*zann*) and definitive proof (*yaqin*) through physical verification, ensuring that women are not burdened by premature invalidation of their worship.
